children.text:
yes I do 100% agree the reason to type the code directly has disappeared.
And I was still wondering what is the worth for us software engineer to make ourself valued than others if we don't type the code anymore.
at the same time applying to new companies somehow still asking to type a code from scratch, it feels confusing and weird since at daily basis we don't do it anymore.

Actually, it seems like the reason to type the code directly has disappeared. In Korea, the computer science field is already experiencing a shortage of new university students, and developers' salaries have been cut by an average of 50%.

children.text: thanks for sharing, I feel so bad last time I was trying to apply for new company and can't properly doing a to type a code from scratch test

I think it's starting to become the new normal. A couple of years ago I was pushing myself to go way out of my way to use AI code assistants in tasks I would never use before. Now I find myself doing the exact same thing but to manually write code.

source.text: I have been working as software engineers for 12 years, and the last 2 years I have been utilize AI for coding, and the last years mostly I don't code or type code anymore, just doing prompt, a review of the generated code, and setting a workflow for agent to spesific task. I just feels I'm starting to lose my basic programming skills to write code from scrath
source.title: Ask HN: Is it normal to not write code for a years as software engineer?
